description: Save who the user wants as customers (or, for a recruiter, as clients) to their Fundz account: industries, locations, company sizes, the events to watch, and the three answers that decide how well the daily leads fit: who buys (buyer_description), three to five example customers (example_customers) and what is not a fit (avoid_companies). The lead scorer reads those three for every company it considers; without a who-buys sentence or at least two example customers Fundz can only match on industry, size and location, and niche buyers get missed. Pass what the user said in their own words as ideal_customer_profile; pass industries, locations and employee_ranges directly when you have them. Send everything you have together in ONE call. On an account with no lead list today, this save starts building the first list straight away from whatever is on file at that moment, so the who-buys answers belong in the same call, not a later one; the result says when the list will be ready (about five minutes) and every later Fundz result reports the build status. Setup counts as complete in the Fundz app (no setup screen on first sign-in) once what the company sells, an industry, a location and either a who-buys sentence of 40+ characters or two example customers are on file; the result says which of these is still missing. What the company sells and the buyer job titles are saved with save_sender_profile, not here. This changes the saved targeting that the daily lead list is scored against, so read back what was saved.

avoid_companies.description: What is NOT a fit, in the user's words: kinds of companies, sectors or named companies to keep out of the list (e.g. "no agencies or consultancies, no public companies, nothing in crypto").

buyer_description.description: Who buys from the user, in their own words: the kind of company, what is usually going on there when they buy, and what sets a real buyer apart from a look-alike (e.g. "Series A to C software companies that just hired their first VP Sales and are building an outbound team"). One to three sentences. Read by the lead scorer for every company.

buying_signals.description: Events that make a company a lead: funding (recent funding), exec_hire (new leadership), product_launch, contract (new contracts), acquisition, sec_filing (SEC 8-K filings), fund_raise (fund formations), hiring_surge, exec_departure (open executive seats), crowdfunding. Leave out to keep what is saved; a new account tracks all of them.

deal_size.description: Typical deal size, one or more of: under_10k, 10k_50k, 50k_250k, over_250k. Optional. It tells the scorer what size of company can afford the user; it never hides a company.

employee_ranges.description: Employee size ranges: range1 (0-50), range2 (51-200), range3 (201-500), range4 (501-1000), range5 (1001-5000), range6 (5000+)

example_customers.description: Three to five real customers (company names, or names with a website) the user would like more of. The scorer looks for companies like them. Up to 10.

ideal_customer_profile.description: Natural language description of your ideal customer (e.g., "enterprise software companies in healthcare with 500+ employees")

request_instant_scoring.description: If true, returns instant AI-scored leads matching the new preferences

supply_choice.description: Pass "keep" ONLY after a Fundz result said LEAD SUPPLY with a low number, you told the user that number, and the user said to keep the filters as they are. It records that they chose to keep them knowing how many leads a day to expect. Send it alone, with no other fields. Never pass it without asking the user.
